rules.false_positive_analysis: Advisory: qualified std/core primitive NonZero constructors and literal zero only. Safe constructors, nonzero/computed values, imported/custom modules, raw identifiers and stringify token data stay unresolved or silent.

sources.claim: The unsafe NonZero constructor requires a nonzero value; zero violates Rust's validity contract.
Maps the local validity/trust/resource boundary, not proof of deployed exposure or exploitation.

positive.source: fn build() { let value = unsafe { std::num::NonZeroU32::new_unchecked(0) }; }
fn build() { let value = unsafe { core::num::NonZeroI64::new_unchecked(0) }; }
fn build() { let value = unsafe { std::num::NonZeroU32::new_unchecked(0u32) }; }
fn build() { let value = unsafe { std::num::NonZeroUsize::new_unchecked(0_usize) }; }

negative.source: fn build() { let value = unsafe { std::num::NonZeroU32::new_unchecked(1) }; }
fn build() { let value = unsafe { std::num::NonZeroU32::new(0) }; }
fn build() { let value = unsafe { std::num::NonZeroU32::new_unchecked(value) }; }
fn build() { let value = unsafe { custom::std::num::NonZeroU32::new_unchecked(0) }; }
fn build() { let value = unsafe { std::num::CustomNumber::new_unchecked(0) }; }
fn build() { let value = unsafe { std::num::NonZeroU32::new_unchecked(0.0) }; }
fn build() { let value = unsafe { std::num::NonZeroU32::new_unchecked(0u64) }; }

adversarial.source:
/* fn build() { let value = unsafe { std::num::NonZeroU32::new_unchecked(0) }; }
 */
adversarial.rationale: A comment cannot construct an unsafe integer value or establish reachability.

adversarial.source:
use custom::std;
fn build() { let value = unsafe { std::num::NonZeroU32::new_unchecked(0) }; }
adversarial.rationale: An imported standard-looking module name has unresolved identity, so its constructors are not presumed native.

adversarial.source:
use custom::{core};
fn build() { let value = unsafe { core::num::NonZeroU32::new_unchecked(0) }; }
adversarial.rationale: A grouped import can bind core to a custom module rather than the Rust standard library.

adversarial.source:
mod r#std {}
fn build() { let value = unsafe { std::num::NonZeroU32::new_unchecked(0) }; }
adversarial.rationale: A raw identifier declaration can shadow a standard module spelling and must not establish native identity.

adversarial.source:
const EXAMPLE: &str = stringify!(fn build() { let value = unsafe { std::num::NonZeroU32::new_unchecked(0) }; }
);
adversarial.rationale: stringify consumes token data; a constructor-looking token sequence is not an evaluated call.

rules.false_positive_analysis: Advisory: imported timers or timers/promises and the correct delay position. Only exact decimal integers or bounded products are evaluated. Global/browser timers, other computed delays, callback data, safe limits and ambiguous bindings stay silent.

sources.claim: Node coerces delays greater than 2147483647 milliseconds to one millisecond; callback and promise APIs use different delay positions.
Maps the local validity/trust/resource boundary, not proof of deployed exposure or exploitation.

positive.source:
import {setInterval} from 'node:timers';
setInterval(tick, 2147483648);

import {setTimeout} from 'node:timers';
setTimeout(tick, 2147483648);

import {setInterval as repeat} from 'node:timers';
repeat(tick, 2147483648);

import {setTimeout as wait} from 'node:timers/promises';
await wait(3000000000, 'value');

import {setInterval} from 'node:timers';
setInterval(tick, 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);

const timers = require('node:timers');
timers.setTimeout(tick, 3000000000);

adversarial.rationale: Timer-looking comment text does not create a runtime schedule.
A local parameter shadows the imported timer and invalidates its coercion semantics.
Oversized numeric tokens remain unresolved without unbounded integer conversion or evaluation.
Products outside exact JavaScript integer range are not evaluated into affirmative evidence.

rules.false_positive_analysis: Advisory: import-bound QueuePool constructor with explicit pool_size=0 or max_overflow=-1. Engine defaults, other pool classes, positional/keyword collisions, unknown values and changed/escaped bindings stay silent. QueuePool is not imported or executed by the scanner.

sources.claim: QueuePool defaults are finite; pool_size=0 or max_overflow=-1 explicitly removes a capacity bound.
Maps the local validity/trust/resource boundary, not proof of deployed exposure or exploitation.

positive.source:
from sqlalchemy.pool import QueuePool
pool = QueuePool(connect, pool_size=0)

from sqlalchemy.pool import QueuePool
pool = QueuePool(connect, max_overflow=-1)

from sqlalchemy.pool import QueuePool as Pool
pool = Pool(connect, pool_size=0)

import sqlalchemy.pool as pools
pool = pools.QueuePool(connect, 5, -1)

from sqlalchemy.pool import QueuePool
pool = QueuePool(creator=connect, pool_size=0, max_overflow=10)

A function parameter masks the imported class; its settings need separate review.

rules.false_positive_analysis: Advisory: explicit std/core memory constructors with reference types only. Raw pointers, integers, Option references and MaybeUninit storage stay silent. Imported/custom module paths, raw identifiers, stringify token data and complex types stay unresolved.

sources.claim: Constructing an uninitialized reference violates its initialized-address invariant even if the resulting reference is not used.
Maps the local validity/trust/resource boundary, not proof of deployed exposure or exploitation.

unsafe fn invalid() { let value = core::mem::uninitialized::<&mut u8>(); }
unsafe fn invalid() { let value = std::mem::uninitialized::<&'static str>(); }

let example = stringify!(unsafe fn invalid() { let value = std::mem::uninitialized::<&u32>(); }
);
adversarial.rationale: Token stringification is data, not reference construction; no macro expansion is executed by the scanner.

"#;
adversarial.rationale: A raw Rust string must not be interpreted as a native memory operation.

rules.false_positive_analysis: Self-signed development and explicit trust stores require context. Typed SslStream client options with an unconditional four-parameter validation callback are advisory; custom types, conditional callbacks and changed/escaped receivers stay unresolved. Other language variants retain their own scope.

sources.claim: The callback decides whether to accept the peer certificate; an unconditional true callback ignores reported validation errors.
Maps the local validity/trust/resource boundary, not proof of deployed exposure or exploitation.

positive.source:
using System.Net.Security;
async System.Threading.Tasks.Task Connect(SslStream tls) { await tls.AuthenticateAsClientAsync(new SslClientAuthenticationOptions { TargetHost = host, RemoteCertificateValidationCallback = (sender, cert, chain, errors) => true }); }

using System.Net.Security;
async System.Threading.Tasks.Task Connect(SslStream tls) { await tls.AuthenticateAsClientAsync(new SslClientAuthenticationOptions { TargetHost = host, RemoteCertificateValidationCallback = static (_, _, _, _) => true }); }

using System.Net.Security;
async System.Threading.Tasks.Task Connect(SslStream tls) { await tls.AuthenticateAsClientAsync(new SslClientAuthenticationOptions { TargetHost = host, RemoteCertificateValidationCallback = (sender, cert, chain, errors) => { return true; } }); }
